messages:
mike-b: Quick follow-up from the asyncization + ownership RFC — sketching a smaller, safer cutover for dashboard query batching + affinity. Goals: reduce p99 tail for small interactive dashboards, avoid overloading the general executor, and keep RBAC checks cheap.
leah-p: +1 on reducing p99. can you outline the ownership boundaries you have in mind?
samir: I want to avoid new global state if possible. What does "affinity" mean here? per-tenant? per-panel-type?
mike-b: Affinity = session affinity for short lived requests that benefit from warm KV/cache + batching. Key idea: maintain a labeled executor pool (fast-path) that prefers requests with the same affinity key so they can reuse warmed caches and batching windows. Affinity key proposal: tenant_id + route + query_shape_hash.
chen: query_shape_hash sounds expensive to compute for every request. How stable is it?
mike-b: It'd be a cheap fingerprint of the AST shape (not full query). The pipeline already normalizes query AST for caching. We can reuse that pass. Fingerprint cost ~ <1ms typical.
leah-p: How does RBAC interact? We can't defer auth checks to the fast-path unless we ensure isolation.
samir: Two options: 1) auth at edge (preferred) before affinity assignment, only authorized requests hit fast-path; 2) auth inside executor but with a tiny capability token so check is constant time. Edge auth reduces per-executor complexity.
mike-b: I'm leaning toward edge auth + attach a signed short-lived "capability" header (HMAC over tenant+route+ts) that fast-path verifies (cheap). If verification fails, route to general pool.
chen: Sounds good. What about slow queries that accidentally get the affinity key and clog the fast-path?
mike-b: We'll have a heuristic: max_tokens and estimated_cost thresholds. Also use a rolling token bucket per-affinity with fast-fail to general pool when exceeded. If a job exceeds tokencount budget, kick it to background async queue.
samir: We should be explicit about SLOs and metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency for fast-path vs general pool, affinity cache-hit-rate, batch sizes, and "leaked" slow requests count.
leah-p: Can we see a minimal config snippet that ops can toggle? would like feature flag + rollout plan.
mike-b: Sure — example config idea:

```yaml
fast_path:
  enabled: false  # feature flag
  affinity_key: tenant:route:shape_hash
  max_tokens: 4096
  max_est_cost_ms: 50
  per_affinity_bucket_qps: 10
  verify_capability_header: true

routing:
  fallback_pool: general-executor
  async_queue: background-renderers
  canary_pct: 1
```

mike-b: Rollout sketch: enable=false default. Enable behind org-level feature flag. Start canary at 1% with strict metrics alerting. If stable, increase to 10% then 50% over 2 weeks.
chen: Ops-wise: need to monitor executor utilization and cache eviction rates. Also add alerts for affinity bucket exhaustion (rapid 429s).
samir: For DB/RPC cost: affinity increases cache reuse but may increase tail latency when one affinity dominates. We should implement backpressure across affinity buckets: global concurrency cap that we can bump.
leah-p: What's the migration path for old dashboards? Do we need a migration of saved queries or will the system work transparently?
mike-b: Transparent — affinity is assigned at request time via fingerprint. Saved queries keep working. We do need to add a small migration to bake the fingerprint for warmup jobs for high-frequency dashboards (crons) — that's optional.
chen: Can we lazy-warm caches when we detect a hot affinity? e.g., background warmup job that primes KV for that affinity when traffic > threshold.
mike-b: Yes — plan: hot-signal detector emits "hot_affinity" events to the background warmers. Warmers can prefetch KV prefixes and warm model KV caches. We'll measure warmup time (ms) and hit-rate improvement.
samir: One more: observability hooks — we need per-affinity trace ids propagated for debugging. Also make sure RBAC traces include which layer verified auth (edge vs executor).
mike-b: Agreed. Also propose adding a small rollout checklist to console doc: stats to watch: p99 fast_path latency, fast_path cache hit-rate, general pool p99, error rate delta, 5xxs, 429s from bucket throttle, and CPU/GPU hot shards.
leah-p: Sounds actionable. Can you write a short RFC follow-up (1 pager) with the config, rollout plan, and runbook items? I'll route to security for the capability header threat model.
mike-b: Will do.
deploy-bot: mike-b requested review from @security-team at 1718234600
chen: one last ops note — add a maintenance mode toggle to drain fast-path (route all to general) for quick rollback.
mike-b: Good call. Adding drain toggle.
leah-p: Thanks everyone. No blockers from product.
